title: Quotient stacks commute with invariant base change
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks, Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces and 2-fibre products have the meanings of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over $S$, meaning that functorially on test schemes its objects and arrows form a groupoid, with the laws of [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]. Let $a:U\to X$ be a map to an algebraic space with $as=at$. For any algebraic-space map $X_1\to X$, put $U_1=U\times_XX_1$ and $R_1=R\times_XX_1$ with all groupoid maps obtained by base change. If $[U/R]$ and $[U_1/R_1]$ denote the fppf stackifications of their groupoid prestacks [def-pc-fppf-site], the canonical square with top row $[U_1/R_1]\to[U/R]$ and bottom row $X_1\to X$ is 2-cartesian. The vertical maps are induced by $a$ and its base change.

proof.text: Write $A=[U/R]$, $A_1=[U_1/R_1]$, $g:X_1\to X$, and let $\iota,\iota_1$ be the maps from the two groupoid prestacks to their stackifications. An algebraic space is an fppf sheaf; regarded as a discrete fibred groupoid it is a stack, since objects glue by the sheaf axiom and all arrows are identities. The invariant map $a$ sends every arrow of the groupoid prestack to an identity in $X$. The stackification extension property therefore gives $f:A\to X$ and likewise $f_1:A_1\to X_1$. Put $B=X_1\times_X A$. By the definition of the 2-fibre product, $B(T)$ consists of pairs $(x_1,y)$ with $g x_1=f(y)$, and arrows are arrows in $A(T)$ with the same $x_1$. This fibred groupoid is a stack: for covering descent data, glue the $x_1$ components in the sheaf $X_1$ and the $y$ components in the stack $A$; their equality in $X$ holds locally and hence globally. Arrows glue uniquely by the isomorphism-sheaf axiom for $A$. The maps on the groupoid prestack $(u,x_1)\mapsto(x_1,\iota(u))$ and $(r,x_1)\mapsto \iota(r)$ preserve composition and pullback. Extending this functor to the stack $B$ gives $F:A_1\to B$ whose composite with $\iota_1$ is isomorphic to it. Its first component equals $f_1$: both send $\iota_1(u,x_1)$ to $x_1$, since $X_1$ has only identity arrows and the base change $U_1\to X_1$ of $a$ is the projection; every object of $A_1$ is locally of this form, and $X_1$ is a sheaf. Its second component $h$ satisfies $h\iota_1\cong\iota p$ for the projection $p:(u,x_1)\mapsto u$, $(r,x_1)\mapsto r$ of groupoid prestacks, so $h$ is an extension of $\iota p$ as given by the extension property; it is the top map $[U_1/R_1]\to[U/R]$, and $fh=gf_1$ because $F$ lands in $B$. Thus $F=(f_1,h)$ is the canonical comparison of the square with the 2-fibre product.

proof.text: For $u,v\in U(T)$, the presheaf of arrows from $u$ to $v$ is $V\mapsto\{r\in R(V):s(r)=u|_V,\ t(r)=v|_V\}$. It is an fppf sheaf: local arrows glue uniquely in the sheaf $R$, and their endpoint equations hold after gluing since $U$ is a sheaf. The same argument applies to $U_1,R_1$, whose sections are compatible pairs of sections. Sheafification fixes a sheaf: its universal property applied to its own identity gives an inverse to the unit, and uniqueness gives both inverse identities. Thus the isomorphism-sheaf clause of stackification identifies arrows between chart objects in $A$ and $A_1$ with these original arrow sheaves. For $u_1=(u,x_1)$ and $v_1=(v,z_1)$, an arrow between their images in $B$ requires $x_1=z_1$ and an $r$ with endpoints $u,v$. If $x_1=z_1$, invariance gives $a s(r)=a(u)=g x_1$, so the unique compatible pair $(r,x_1)$ is an $R_1$-arrow with endpoints $u_1,v_1$. Conversely every such $R_1$-arrow projects to this $r$ and forces $x_1=z_1$. These inverse rules commute with restriction, composition, identities and inverses because the operations on $R_1$ are the base-changed operations, with unchanged $X_1$ component. Hence $F$ induces bijections on all arrow sheaves between chart objects.

proof.text: Let $z,w\in A_1(T)$. The local-object clause of stackification supplies an fppf cover on which both are isomorphic to chart objects; take the common refinement of the two covers. Conjugating by these isomorphisms identifies the map of isomorphism sheaves induced by $F$ with the bijections of step 2 on this cover. Given a target arrow over $T$, the local inverse arrows agree on overlaps by local injectivity, and glue uniquely because $A_1$ is a stack. Their image equals the given arrow since this holds on the cover and $B$ is a stack. Likewise two arrows with the same image coincide locally and hence globally. Thus every fibre functor $F_T$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Tag 0DTG, lemma-base-change-quotient-stack, proof; explicit morphism verification using stacks.tex Tags 02ZP/0436 and spaces-groupoids.tex Tag 044X.

proof.text: For an object $(x_1,y)\in B(T)$ choose an fppf cover $T_i\to T$ and isomorphisms $\iota(u_i)\cong y|_{T_i}$ using the local-object clause for $A$. Applying $f$ to these isomorphisms gives $a(u_i)=g(x_1|_{T_i})$, since $X$ has only identity arrows. Hence $u_{1,i}=(u_i,x_1|_{T_i})$ is a section of $U_1$. Its image under $F$ is isomorphic to $(x_1,y)|_{T_i}$, with isomorphism given by the chosen one in $A$ and the identity on $x_1|_{T_i}$. Thus $F$ is locally essentially surjective. In the descent-data notation of 0DTG these are precisely the lifts $u_i\mapsto(u_i,x_1)$ and $r_{ij}\mapsto(r_{ij},x_1)$; step 2 also verifies their arrow compatibility, which the source leaves implicit.

source.place: Tag 0DTG, lemma-base-change-quotient-stack, proof; explicit morphism verification using stacks.tex Tags 02ZP/0436 and spaces-groupoids.tex Tag 044X.

proof.text: Both $A_1$ and $B$ are stacks on the same big fppf site in the stipulated universes. Step 3 gives fibrewise full faithfulness and step 4 gives covering-local essential surjectivity. Apply the fully faithful local-equivalence criterion to obtain an equivalence $A_1\simeq B$ over that site. Since $F$ is the comparison to the 2-fibre product of step 1, this says exactly that the displayed canonical square is 2-cartesian, with the indicated vertical maps.
